blocks.text: Most social media managers do not spend their day on social. That is the first thing to accept, and it explains a lot of the tiredness. Hootsuite's 2023 Social Media Career Report found that most people who work in social media spend less than half their day on it.
Where a social media manager's day goes

Survey numbers make a useful map. They do not tell you about your Tuesday. Use them to see the pattern, then check your own calendar for a week. Write down every task you touch, including the tiny ones.

Hootsuite's teams and tasks page says the average social marketer does about eight different jobs. Those jobs include copywriting, photo and video production, post scheduling, ad creation, strategy, analytics, social listening and influencer management. Two-thirds say they have too many things to do.

Sprout Social's Social Media Productivity Report surveyed over 500 social marketers in the US and UK. It found that 48% feel they sometimes or rarely have enough time to get their work done. The page gives no survey date and no hours per task, so read it as a sign of pressure, not a timesheet.

The big jobs are easy to name. The small ones are harder to see. Resizing one graphic for several platforms, finding a clause in a contract and rewriting a caption again all count. Each one pulls you out of the thread you were in. That switching is where many afternoons go.

Email and chat take their share too. Microsoft's June 2025 study, based on a survey of 31,000 knowledge workers in 31 markets, reports 117 emails and 153 Teams messages a day for the average employee. Those figures cover all office roles, not social managers alone. They still show how much of your day can go to the inbox.
Which AI tools for social media managers fit each job

Pick AI tools by job, not by brand. A caption writer, a design app, a scheduler, a chat app and a voice helper each solve a different problem. Start with the slowest part of your week, then find the tool that fits it. Most managers need only a few of these, not every app on the list.

How to draft captions with AI without losing your brand voice

Captions are the first job most people hand to AI. Give the tool three things: the brand voice in plain words, the goal of the post, and one example you already like. Without those, every draft sounds the same. Your feed then sounds like everyone else's.

Here is a worked example. You run social for a coffee roaster. The post launches a new Ethiopian blend. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and say: 'Draft three captions for the new Ethiopian blend. Warm, short, no emoji, mention the tasting notes.' Lazur reads the drafts out loud. You pick one, and Lazur can type the draft at your cursor.

Then hold fn and dictate your own edits. Speaking edits can keep the wording closer to how your brand talks. Read the final caption out loud once before you schedule it. Odd phrasing shows up fast when you hear it.

Check every fact before it goes live. If a caption names a price, a delivery time or a result, find the source first. AI tools guess when they do not know. Keep the source link in the post notes, so the next editor can check it too.
How to resize and fix graphics in Canva on Mac

Canva has a native Mac app. Canva's download page says the desktop app runs on Macs with Intel and Apple chips. If you open the same files all day, use the desktop app and keep the browser for quick checks. For a deeper walkthrough, see [Canva for social media managers on Mac](/for/social-media-managers/canva).

Resizing is where small minutes pile up. One square post often needs a vertical version, a wide link card and a banner. Canva can make the copies, but the setting is easy to miss when you are tired. Ask Lazur where it is, and it circles the control on your screen and labels it.

Here is a worked example. You have a square post, and the client wants a vertical story next. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask: 'Walk me through resizing this design to a vertical story.' Lazur guides you one click at a time and waits for each click before it moves on. You keep the mouse, and you keep the choice.

The common mistake is trusting the resized copy. Text can crop, overflow or land on top of a logo at the new size. Open each version and check it at full zoom before you export. Ask Lazur to point at a text box that looks wrong, and it will circle it.
Slack threads and approvals on Mac

Many teams run client approvals in Slack. Slack's download page lists the current Mac desktop version as 4.53.280 at the time it was checked. If your app looks older, check your version under Slack > About Slack. An old app can miss features that the help pages describe.

Busy channels bury the one message you need. Press ⌘K to jump to a conversation by name. Use the Threads view to find replies you still owe. The guides on [how to view threads in Slack on Mac](/how-to/open-the-threads-view-in-slack) and [how to jump to the latest unread message in Slack on Mac](/how-to/jump-to-the-latest-unread-message-in-slack) cover the steps.

Lazur helps when the thread is long. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and say: 'What does the designer need from me before noon?' Lazur reads the thread on your screen and answers out loud. It does not reply for you. Dictate your answer with fn, then read it before you send.
Keep client accounts apart in Chrome

Most social managers switch between client logins all day. Chrome profiles keep each client in its own window, with its own history, cookies and signed-in accounts. The setup takes a few minutes. The full walkthrough is in [Chrome for social media managers on Mac](/for/social-media-managers/chrome).

The mistake to avoid is posting from the wrong account. It happens when two business tabs look almost the same. Give each profile a clear name and a different avatar. Check the account name in the page header before you publish. Ask Lazur to point at the profile avatar if you lose track of which window you are in.
Run competitor research in the background

Competitor checks eat afternoons. Lazur can run research in its own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. You keep working while the job runs, and you read the result when it is ready.

Write the brief like a task for a junior colleague. For example: 'Look at the last two weeks of posts from these accounts. List the formats, the posting days and any giveaways. Give me a summary and a report.' Name the accounts and the time window, so the search stays narrow.
Check the report before you act on it. Posts get deleted, hidden or restricted, and a search can miss them. Treat the report as a starting point for your own look at the accounts.
Client data, brand rules and what not to paste

Your client contracts and your agency rules come first. Before you paste an analytics export, an unreleased campaign plan or a customer's messages into any AI tool, check what those rules allow. If you are not sure, ask your manager or your legal team before you share it.

Here is how Lazur handles data, as the product describes it. It listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Those are product statements, not a compliance certificate. Decide with your own rules in front of you.

Mistakes social media managers make with AI

items: Publishing the first draft. Read each caption out loud before it goes live.
Trusting a figure without a source. Open the original page and check the number before it goes in a post.
Letting every account sound alike. Give the tool two real posts from the brand as examples.
Asking for testimonials that customers never gave. Do not have an AI write quotes and attach a customer's name.
Forgetting platform disclosure rules. Check each network's help center for paid partnership and ad labels.
Skipping the handoff. Tell your designer or client what you changed and why, in one line.

blocks.text: Is speaking faster than typing for your drafts?

Some managers find that short replies are faster by voice, and long edits are still easier by keyboard. Test it on your own work. Try the [speaking vs typing test](/tools/speaking-vs-typing-test) for a quick comparison, and run the same caption both ways.

If you want to check your typing speed first, try the [typing speed test](/tools/typing-speed-test). Compare the result with how fast you dictate a real caption. Results differ by task, so use your own work as the test.
When you are ready, [see the pricing page](/pricing) to compare plans. Start with the trial, use it on one job, and decide from your own week.

faq.question: What are the best AI tools for social media managers on Mac?
faq.answer: There is no single best tool. Most managers use a caption writer, a design app such as Canva, a scheduler and a chat app. Lazur covers the layer between them, helping you find controls, read threads and draft text by voice. Check each vendor's own site for current pricing and Mac support, since both change.

faq.question: Does Lazur post or schedule social media content for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. It explains, points, guides you one click at a time, drafts and types text, dictates, runs research and handles everyday jobs such as timers and reminders.

faq.question: Is Lazur a plugin for Canva, Slack or Chrome?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnership with any app maker. It works from the screen in front of you, and it answers out loud when you hold the shortcut.

faq.question: Does Lazur watch my screen all the time?
faq.answer: No. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored.

faq.question: Can I use AI tools with client data?
faq.answer: Follow your employer's rules and your clients' contracts first. Lazur's data handling is described above, but that description is not a compliance certification. Ask before you share client files, analytics exports or private messages.

faq.question: How accurate are AI-written captions?
faq.answer: Quality depends on your prompt and your examples. Treat every draft as a first pass. Check facts, numbers and claims against the source, and read the caption out loud before you publish.

faq.question: Which Macs does Lazur run on?
faq.answer: Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. A Windows version is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: How old are the Hootsuite numbers?
faq.answer: Hootsuite's 2023 career report was based on surveys conducted in March and April 2023. The figures may be dated, so read them as a rough guide, not a current benchmark.
